forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: South Derbyshire's audit team faces staffing pressures with recommendations from 2021/22 unresolved
news_drafts.lead: South Derbyshire Council's internal audit team is managing staffing pressure by using external associates to fill gaps, rather than more costly agency staff. Onboarding these associates has proved lengthy, with the council facing challenges around gaining system access for the new team members. Eight audits were completed this year with 24 recommendations made. Yet audit recommendations from 2021/22 remain unresolved, with the internal auditor referring to moderate and low-risk issues with the council's controls and procedures from these earlier audits still being outstanding. These represent actions, the auditor confirmed, that management continues to work on.

findings.paper_title: COUNCIL PLAN 2024-2028 PERFORMANCE REPORT (2026-2027 QUARTER 2 – 1 APRIL TO 30 SEPTEMBER 2026)
findings.headline: 88% of Council Plan measures and projects are reported as on track to achieve their target, across all four priorities
findings.detail: The overall summary table shows 32 green, 8 amber, 6 red and 3 grey across 49 measures and projects. The report gives 88% as the share on track but does not explain how that figure is derived from the table's counts.
findings.matters: A reader comparing councils' performance reporting will want to know how the headline figure is calculated before relying on it.
findings.figures: 88%; 32 green, 8 amber, 6 red, 3 grey; 49 measures and projects in total
findings.quote: 88% of the measures and projects in the Council Plan are on track to achieve the target.

findings.paper_title: COUNCIL PLAN 2024-2028 PERFORMANCE REPORT (2026-2027 QUARTER 2 – 1 APRIL TO 30 SEPTEMBER 2026)
findings.headline: TC1.9, the rolling programme of stock condition surveys, is reported as not meeting its target, one of four measures in the committee's remit that did not
findings.detail: The report lists four measures or projects within the committee's remit as not meeting target and marks them red. TC1.9 is one of these. The paper gives no figures or service commentary for it in the body and refers readers to the appendices.
findings.matters: Stock condition surveys underpin the investment planning for housing stock, so a missed survey programme affects the quality of the capital data behind housing spending decisions.
findings.figures: 4 of 13 measures or projects in the committee's remit did not meet target
findings.quote: TC1.9 Undertake a rolling programme of stock condition surveys.

findings.paper_title: COUNCIL PLAN 2024-2028 PERFORMANCE REPORT (2026-2027 QUARTER 2 – 1 APRIL TO 30 SEPTEMBER 2026)
findings.headline: South Derbyshire reports it is in a holding position on local government reorganisation after a 29 October government announcement, with a further MHCLG update expected in early 2027
findings.detail: The report says there are no direct reorganisation implications for delivering the Council Plan at the time of reporting. It then states that the 29 October announcement put the council in a holding position while Government reconsiders the proposals, and that a new decision will need to be made.
findings.matters: A finance director, here or at a peer council, needs to know that the council's structure and future are unresolved, since reorganisation would change the body that holds the debt, reserves and contracts.
findings.figures: 29 October announcement; MHCLG update expected early 2027
findings.quote: However, following the 29 October announcement on the outcome of the governments rapid review of local government reorganisation we are now in a holding position while Government considers the proposals again.

findings.headline: The Council says the revised policy will support its effort to improve on the Regulator of Social Housing's C3 rating
findings.detail: The Head of Housing states that the policy will give the Regulator of Social Housing further evidence as the Council seeks to improve on a C3 rating it has been issued. The paper does not give the detail of the rating or the grounds for it.
findings.matters: A regulatory grading on a landlord's service is a signal a lender or finance director would track, and the paper ties this policy directly to the grading.
findings.quote: The Policy will provide further evidence to the Regulator of Social Housing as we look to improve on the C3 rating issued.

findings.headline: The Council's £25 cap on discretionary payments is deleted and replaced with severity-based awards
findings.detail: The previous Section 4.5.2 text stated that discretionary payments should not normally exceed £25. The revised policy removes that wording and states that awards will be set by the severity of the maladministration, the impact on the tenant and the Ombudsman guidance in force at the time. The new delay and distress ranges run from £50 to £100 up to £1,000+.
findings.matters: Removing a fixed cap on discretionary payments changes the upper bound on the Council's compensation exposure per case, which a finance director would need to reflect in forecasting.
findings.figures: £25 cap deleted; delay and distress ranges of £50 to £100, £100 to £600, £600 to £1,000+, and £1,000+
findings.quote: Awards will be determined according to the severity of the maladministration, the impact on the tenant and Housing Ombudsman guidance in force at the time of assessment.
